title: The Missionary Purpose
focus: Practice topic: explaining the doctrine of Christ
intro: Missionary work is more than a list of tasks. In this lesson each learner sees its true purpose: to invite people to come to Christ, and to help them receive the restored gospel through faith in Jesus Christ, repentance, baptism, the gift of the Holy Ghost and enduring to the end.
preparation: Study 2 Nephi 31:10–21, 3 Nephi 11:31–41 and 3 Nephi 27:13–21. Write the missionary purpose on the board before class. Ask one learner to prepare a short devotional: a prayer, a hymn and a thought from scripture. Pray for each learner by name.

sections.title: The purpose of missionary work
paras: Ask learners to list what missionaries do each day, and write the list on the board. Then read the missionary purpose together: to invite others to come unto Christ by helping them receive the restored gospel through faith in Jesus Christ and His Atonement, repentance, baptism, the gift of the Holy Ghost and enduring to the end.

Ask: How does this purpose give meaning to the daily tasks? Which part belongs to the missionary, and which part belongs to the person being taught? How would keeping this purpose in mind change the way you serve?

Read this from Elder Dallin H. Oaks, “The Purpose of Missionary Work,” missionary satellite broadcast, April 1995: “We invite all to come unto Christ by repentance and baptism and confirmation in order to open the doors of the celestial kingdom to the sons and daughters of God.” Ask why the aim is greater than adding names to Church records, and read 3 Nephi 11:33–34 together.

sections.title: The doctrine of Christ
paras: Make three groups. One studies 2 Nephi 31:10–21, one studies 3 Nephi 11:31–41 and one studies 3 Nephi 27:13–21. Each group lists what a follower of Christ is asked to do, and then adds its list to the board under the reference.

Draw out two parts. First, what Christ does to draw us to the Father (see Alma 33:22 and Doctrine and Covenants 76:40–42). Second, what we do to receive His blessings: have faith, repent, be baptized, receive the gift of the Holy Ghost and endure to the end (see 3 Nephi 27:16–21). The Lord also said the Book of Mormon would bring to light the true points of His doctrine (Doctrine and Covenants 10:62).

Ask: How would you explain the doctrine of Christ to someone who has never heard it? Why do missionaries teach people who already believe in Christ? Then help learners say this truth: missionaries fulfill their purpose by helping people accept the doctrine of Christ.

sections.title: Helping others act in faith
paras: What a missionary says matters, but what a person does with it matters more. Ask: What shows that someone is growing in faith, repenting and preparing for baptism? What shows that the Holy Ghost was present in a lesson?

Let learners work in pairs. Each tells the other what makes it hard to invite someone to make a commitment, and what would give them confidence. Ask how knowing the doctrine of Christ helps them invite with love.

sections.title: The greatest duty
paras: Read Doctrine and Covenants 18:10 and Doctrine and Covenants 18:15–16. Ask learners to find the blessings that come to those who share the gospel and to those who accept it.

Missionary work is hard. Elder Jeffrey R. Holland said, “I am convinced that missionary work is not easy because salvation is not a cheap experience” (“Missionary Work and the Atonement,” Ensign, March 2001). Ask: How will this help you when the work is hard?

steps.why: Teach the idea and why it matters for a missionary.

examples.title: Say the purpose in your own words
examples.text: Read the missionary purpose aloud. Ask learners to say it in one sentence of their own. Then show the two parts: what the missionary does, and what the person taught is invited to do.

examples.title: Show the doctrine of Christ in steps
examples.text: Draw five steps on the board: faith in Jesus Christ, repentance, baptism, the gift of the Holy Ghost, enduring to the end. Read 3 Nephi 27:16–21 and show where each step appears.

examples.title: Compare two lists
examples.text: Put the list of missionary tasks next to the purpose. Ask learners to show how each task serves the purpose, and which task could become empty if the purpose is forgotten.

steps.why: Show one example of what learners will do.

examples.title: Teach the doctrine of Christ in two minutes
examples.text: Teach one learner the doctrine of Christ using 3 Nephi 11:31–41. Say what Christ asks, say why it matters and invite a response. Keep it plain.

examples.title: Show a kind invitation
examples.text: Show how to invite a friend to pray about the Book of Mormon. Use clear words, a warm voice and a specific time to follow up.

examples.title: Think aloud on a hard question
examples.text: Answer this question aloud: Why do missionaries teach people who already believe in Christ? Use the doctrine of Christ in your answer.

steps.why: Learners practise in pairs or small groups.

examples.title: Explain in pairs
examples.text: Learners work in pairs. Each explains the doctrine of Christ to a friend in two minutes, using one of the three passages. The partner listens as the friend.

examples.title: Invitation role play
examples.text: In pairs, one learner invites the other to read the Book of Mormon. The other shares a real concern. The first listens and answers with love. Then they swap.

examples.title: Write and share your reason
examples.text: Each learner writes why they want to serve and compares it with the missionary purpose. Then they share one change they will make with a partner.

steps.why: Name what went well and what can improve.

examples.title: Partner feedback
examples.text: The learner who was taught says what was clearest and what felt most sincere. The teacher writes one thing to keep and one to improve.

examples.title: Three questions
examples.text: Ask: What went well? What would you change? What helped the listener most to understand the doctrine of Christ? Begin with the good.

examples.title: Simple checklist
examples.text: Was it simple? Was a scripture used and explained? Was the listener invited to act? Did the teacher speak with sincerity?

steps.why: Practise again with what was learned.

examples.title: Switch roles
examples.text: The learner who listened now teaches. Leave time for feedback both ways, and then ask a few to share what they learned.

examples.title: Improve one thing
examples.text: Each learner teaches again and changes one thing: a clearer sentence, a better question or a warmer invitation.

examples.title: Teach a new partner
examples.text: Find a new partner. Teach the same lesson again in two minutes. Share one insight with the class.

testimony: Invite learners to share what they feel about missionary work. Then give your own testimony that learning and living the doctrine of Christ makes a missionary more able to bless others.

tips.text: Open with a short learner-led devotional: a prayer, a hymn and a thought from scripture.
Leave quiet time for learners to ponder and write what they will do.
Ask learners to explain a doctrine in simple words, and to say why it matters.
Greet each learner by name as they arrive.

quote.text: We invite all to come unto Christ by repentance and baptism and confirmation in order to open the doors of the celestial kingdom to the sons and daughters of God.
quote.by: Elder Dallin H. Oaks, “The Purpose of Missionary Work,” missionary satellite broadcast, April 1995

study: Read 3 Nephi 11:33–34 together and ask what it teaches about why we preach the gospel.
invitations: Share with others, in person or online, why you want to serve a mission and what you are doing to prepare.
Invite a friend to come to this class with you.
Invite a friend who is not a member, or who is less active, to be taught the missionary lessons.

blocks.text: Keep the review short. Let two or three learners share, and thank each one.
Welcome the class warmly. Begin with a prayer and a short thought from scripture to invite the Holy Ghost.
Try saying: “Before we start, who would like to tell us what happened when they tried last week’s invitation?”
Read the introduction aloud slowly. Then ask one learner to say it again in their own words.

Missionary work is more than a list of tasks. In this lesson each learner sees its true purpose: to invite people to come to Christ, and to help them receive the restored gospel through faith in Jesus Christ, repentance, baptism, the gift of the Holy Ghost and enduring to the end.
Try saying: “Today we will learn, practise and then teach what we learned. Every one of you will teach.”
Ask learners to say the purpose in one sentence. A short sentence is easier to remember.

Ask why the aim is greater than adding names to Church records, and read 3 Nephi 11:33–34 together.
Listen for: invite, come unto Christ, restored gospel, faith, Atonement.
Say: “A missionary’s purpose is to invite people to come unto Christ. I do this so you can feel the joy I feel.”
Let groups report one at a time, then add what they missed.

How to run it: show one example first, then let pairs try it. Keep it to a few minutes and thank each learner.

Second, what we do to receive His blessings: have faith, repent, be baptized, receive the gift of the Holy Ghost and endure to the end (see 3 Nephi 27:16–21). Listen for: what a follower of Christ does, and what the Savior and the Father promise in return.
Draw four steps on the board: faith, repentance, baptism, the gift of the Holy Ghost. Say: “Each step leads to the next.”
Pair each invitation with a time and a place. A clear invitation is easier to accept.
What a missionary says matters, but what a person does with it matters more.
What shows that someone is growing in faith, repenting and preparing for baptism?
What shows that the Holy Ghost was present in a lesson?
Let learners work in pairs. Each tells the other what makes it hard to invite someone to make a commitment, and what would give them confidence.
Ask how knowing the doctrine of Christ helps them invite with love.
Listen for: a person acts, the Spirit confirms, and the missionary invites again.
Say to a friend: “Would you read this chapter tonight and tell me tomorrow what you felt?”
Ask learners to write the name of one person they will help this month.
Read Doctrine and Covenants 18:10 and Doctrine and Covenants 18:15–16.
Ask learners to find the blessings that come to those who share the gospel and to those who accept it.

Missionary work is hard. Elder Jeffrey R. Holland said, “I am convinced that missionary work is not easy because salvation is not a cheap experience” (“Missionary Work and the Atonement,” Ensign, March 2001).
How will this help you when the work is hard?
Listen for: the worth of souls, joy for the one who shares and the one who receives.
Say: “Helping one person come to Christ is worth more than anything I could do alone.”
